findings.title: Guest avatar routes start hosted runtime bootstrap before ingress/deployment validation, unlike the guest draft route
findings.line: guest-avatar-runtime.ts: `if(phase6Requested())return (await hostedPreviewRuntime())!.avatar;`; guest-avatar-http.ts: `const b=await boundary();if(!b)return empty();await b.guard(req);`
findings.counterexample: The guest draft route (apps/web/src/app/api/guest/[[...record]]/route.ts) calls `hostedPreviewRequestOrigin(r)` (Host/x-vercel-deployment-url/hostname-pattern check) BEFORE calling `hostedPreviewRuntime()`. The avatar routes (`/api/guest/avatar/...`, `/guest-avatar-media/...`) call `boundary()`→`hostedPreviewRuntime()` first (which performs assertNoHostedPlatformContradiction, 6 pool creations, per-service TLS proof and DB-identity SQL) and only invoke the per-request ingress check (`vercelPreviewPeer`→`hostedPreviewRequestOrigin`) afterward, inside `b.guard(req)`.
findings.impact: A request reaching this deployment with a mismatched Host/deployment-URL header (e.g., unexpected alias, proxy misconfiguration, or a cold-instance probe hitting the avatar path first) forces full hosted-runtime bootstrap (6 Postgres pools + TLS handshakes + identity queries) before being rejected, instead of failing fast on ingress mismatch as the draft route does. On serverless cold starts this can be repeated per new instance, and it breaks the intended 'ingress validation before any privileged operation' ordering that the review explicitly requires. Data access itself is not exposed (guard() still throws before `load()`), so this is not a BLOCKER/HIGH.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: In `guestAvatarBoundary()` (or in `guestAvatarHandler` before calling `boundary()`), validate `hostedPreviewRequestOrigin(request)` (or equivalent Vercel ingress check) BEFORE invoking `hostedPreviewRuntime()`, mirroring the ordering already used in the guest draft route.
findings.required_proof: Add a regression test analogous to 'Guest route rejects mismatched deployment ingress before startup IO' (tests/unit/hosted-preview-runtime.test.ts) but for the avatar GET routes, asserting `globalThis.poolCreates===0` when Host/x-vercel-deployment-url is mismatched.

findings.title: Node engine pin loosened from exact patch to minor-range
findings.counterexample: Root and webhook-ingress package.json now accept any Node 24.x instead of pinning 24.15.x; CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) still pins node-version 24.15.0 so this is currently masked, but local/Vercel builds without that exact pin could diverge.
findings.impact: Minor reproducibility/supply-chain drift risk for non-CI builds (e.g., Vercel's own Node runtime selection); no direct security exploit path identified.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Restore an exact/narrow patch pin (e.g., "24.15.x") for both package.json files unless the broader range is a deliberate, documented decision tied to Vercel's runtime support matrix.
findings.required_proof: Confirm Vercel's actual resolved Node version for both projects matches the CI-verified 24.15.0 baseline.

findings.title: Migration 0031's initial immutability guard was weaker than 0032's, within the same changeset
findings.line: 0031 avatar_visual_guard(): `IF NEW.id<>OLD.id OR NEW.created_at<>OLD.created_at THEN RAISE EXCEPTION`; 0032 CREATE OR REPLACE compares the full immutable-column ROW.
findings.counterexample: Between 0031 and 0032 applied as separate statements, a row UPDATE changing layer/model_id/variant_id/season/ski_length_cm/media_id/derivative_sha256/revision_id/release_id would not have been blocked by 0031's original guard alone.
findings.impact: No live exploitability: both migrations are always applied together (sequential migration runner, single deploy), so at runtime only 0032's final, correct guard is ever active. This is only a design-hygiene note for auditors reading the 0031 diff in isolation.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: None required for this integration; optionally add a comment in 0031 noting the guard is intentionally superseded by 0032 in the same release.
findings.required_proof: Confirm the migration runner applies 0031 and 0032 atomically/sequentially with no gap where 0031-only state is queryable in Production (already true for this local/dev migration path).

correction.evidenceAssessment: Diff and current-file review confirm F1's minimum_safe_correction was applied precisely: guestAvatarBoundary(request) now calls hostedPreviewRequestOrigin(request) before hostedPreviewRuntime(), mirroring the guest draft route, and both avatar route entrypoints thread the real Request through guestAvatarHandler->boundary(req) instead of a no-arg boundary(). The four required regression cases (metadata/media x host/x-vercel-deployment-url mismatch) assert poolCreates===0 and a generic 404 before any DB pool is constructed, and a paired 'exact ingress' case per surface confirms poolCreates===1 and the pre-existing isolated driver failure is still reached only after ingress passes, so no fail-open or bypass was introduced. The per-request guard() path (vercelPreviewPeer/hostedPreviewRequestOrigin) is retained unchanged, giving intentional defense-in-depth rather than a regression. tests/avatar/tier2-rate.ts uses avatarGuestSecurity built from the unmodified production guest.p4-approved-policy.json (only version/peerRequests/globalRequests overridden, preserving underlying window semantics), drives 242 concurrent guard() calls across two independent Pool objects/pg connections against real Postgres, and asserts exactly peerRequests(240) succeed with both the peer- and global-scoped guest_rate_buckets rows converging to 240 -- direct evidence of atomic, cross-pool budget enforcement rather than per-process counting. It further asserts loads===0 and reads===0 while HTTP 429 is returned on both GET surfaces before any load()/reader() call, exercises an unrelated ordinary GuestSecurity.guard() call post-exhaustion succeeding with zero business-table writes (booking-policy isolation), and validates window recovery via an inventory_clock() advance yielding a 200 with load()===1. This is parent-supplied execution evidence (686 unit PASS, avatar suite PASS including the new test now wired into test:avatar/CI, lint/typecheck/build/secrets PASS, 32-migration hash unchanged, browser+real-PG Avatar/Guest PASS) which this review did not re-execute (tests_executed:false); the static code/diff inspection independently corroborates that the described ordering and test assertions are structurally present and internally consistent. The four supplied migration-count assertion diffs (30->32) close the prior static evidence gap without touching historical migration bytes. LOW F2-F4 are unchanged by this diff and remain recorded/nonblocking per the LOW DISPOSITION.
